scope: Restore the Publish 14.1 tame command as a complete phased Creature Handler transaction that converts an eligible wild baby into a persistent callable pet and durable pet control device.

findings: The authoritative client table registers tame to cmdTame with a required other target, 32-meter client maximum, player.skill.taming, and nonqueued dispatch.
outdoors_creaturehandler_novice grants tame, four stored pets, one active creature, tame_non_aggro 5, and tame_level 12.
The retained SOE tree contains tameability/chance/control-cap policy plus complete PCD save, store, recall, command-list, callable-link, growth, and pet scripts, but no cmdTame transaction.

Pinned Core3 evidence establishes admission within 8 meters, three utterances over 30 seconds, final chance resolution, rollback/optional aggression, PCD materialization, baby growth stage, follow behavior, persistence, and 20 times creature-level XP.

productionContract.exclusiveTransaction: player and target script-variable locks prevent overlapping tame attempts
productionContract.taskReceiver: cmdTame temporarily attaches player.skill.taming_task because command-table dispatch targets are not persistent message receivers
eligibility: living player and living non-player monster baby
not in combat and within 8 meters throughout the transaction
tameable creature-table row with a positive skill-derived chance
Creature Handler novice skill, active/stored capacity, control level, and datapad
final commit revalidates skill, chance, capacity, control level, and datapad
productionContract.failure: release both transaction locks, restore original wild calm behavior, and give aggressive creatures a one-in-twenty retaliation chance
productionContract.success: persist the source creature, create/specify a PCD in the datapad, set growth stage one, convert to ai.pet, link master/PCD/pet, initialize default commands, save pet data, and follow the master
productionContract.crashSafety: a nonpersistent one-second task heartbeat repeatedly calls stop while the transaction lock exists; it never writes a persistent STOP default behavior and all delayed work becomes inert when the lock is cleared

liveFixture.fixtureIsolation: production randomness remains unchanged unless the exact player OID, station ID, protocol, prepared root, and target all match
liveFixture.restartProtocol: PrepareStore leaves a persistent lifecycle/PCD snapshot armed; VerifyRecall runs only after an actual server/client restart and authenticated relogin
liveFixture.ownerContextBridge: the attached fixture polls durable store/call request flags from player context and re-arms its nonpersistent poll on login; ownerless ServerConsole never invokes pet library lifecycle functions
liveFixture.cleanupPolicy: destroy the fixture active pet and PCD, clear callable/tame state, restore creaturehandler XP and skill points, revoke only fixture skills, restore prior pet-master script presence, and prove repeated cleanup is idempotent

liveEvidence.persistenceModel: the stored PCD is durable across restart; recall reconstructs the active pet as an intentionally transient object linked back to that device

production phased tame admission, revalidation, chance, rollback, and XP
persistent baby-pet and PCD materialization with callable links/default commands
authenticated protocol-155 dispatch, storage, restart persistence, recall, cleanup, and health

every tameable species and later Creature Handler training progression
